plot_metadata.caption: Fig. 11. Comparison of corrosion properties between HEAs and conventional alloys [60–66] in the 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. The higher pitting potential $(E _ { \mathrm { p } })$ and lower corrosion-current density $(I _ { \mathrm { c o r r } })$ of Al CoCrFeNi HEAs indicate that the localized and general corrosion-resistant properties of the Al CoCrFeNi HEAs are comparable or even superior to that of conventional corrosion-resistant alloys.
